> **Handoff definition:** one small Owner-approved slice; exact observable success, negative paths, *minimal implementation path*, explicit non-goals, traceability to simple test/evidence, and named dependency/format limits. Antigravity always self-reviews, then independent Codex slice review; three remediation/re-review rounds max. No separate staging review; Owner performs Git staging as part of ordinary commit.

# Executable slice handoff — [phase/slice]

- Status: READY_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION only after pre-handoff approval
- Owner decision / accepted review: [links]
- Implementer: Antigravity
- Reviewer: independent Codex
- Entry commit: [SHA]

## User-visible acceptance (MUST)
| ID | Scenario/input | Expected observable result | Minimal test | Existing reusable implementation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Non-goals (MUST NOT)
[Every unasked feature explicitly excluded.]

## Simplicity decision
[Selected smallest adequate solution; rejected speculative alternative; reasons.]

## Precise change map
[Allowed packages/files/DB/API changes; shared/frozen boundary; deletes if authorized.]

## Negative/failure tests
[Only meaningful changed-boundary security, correctness and recovery cases.]

## Implementation checks
[Focused tests + Antigravity self-review + one independent Codex review; no redundant full-suite loops.]

## Definition of done and handback
[Evidence commands/exits, known limitations, diff list, remaining finding IDs.]

## Blockers/Owner decisions
[Stop rather than guess or auto-expand scope.]
